name: Computability theory (Church-Turing)
summary: Turing defined an abstract machine, computable numbers and a universal machine, answering the Entscheidungsproblem negatively.

name: Computational group theory: computers enter group theory
summary: From Todd-Coxeter coset enumeration to the 1967 Oxford conference, Sims's permutation methods and the Cayley and GAP systems, machine computation became a standard working method of group theory.

name: Shannon switching circuits
summary: Boole's algebra was applied to analyse and simplify relay circuits.

name: Operations research
summary: Wartime scientific analysis of radar and convoys becomes a quantitative decision discipline.

name: Lie-ring methods enter the Burnside problem (Magnus to Zelmanov)
summary: Magnus tied Baker-Hausdorff-type Lie machinery to exponent questions on groups, defining the restricted Burnside problem; this Lie-algebraic route was eventually completed by Zelmanov.

name: Analytic combinatorics: generating functions as complex-analytic objects
summary: Singularities of generating functions determine asymptotics of combinatorial classes, in a systematic symbolic-to-analytic method.

name: Gelfand theory of Banach algebras
summary: Maximal ideals of normed rings gave a topological representation.

name: Statistical decision theory
summary: Estimation and testing recast as games.

name: Wiener-Kolmogorov filtering
summary: Optimal prediction of stationary processes was solved by spectral methods.

name: Kantorovich linear programming
summary: Production-planning problems were posed as linear optimisation with multipliers, with solution methods.
